statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow); Tail is at the top of WATCH while Stress remains extreme.
recommendation: Current evidence supports WATCH-level Tail: NQ remains below settlement but off the session low, while weak semiconductors, elevated Treasury yields, oil above $100 and the approaching PPI window keep risk sensitivity high.
headline: WATCH Tail as NQ stays off the low ahead of PPI
body: Delayed September NQ is 29,396.25, 52.5 points below prior settlement after a 29,359.25–29,508.25 session range. The roughly 37-point recovery from the low shows mean reversion remains present. Fresh supplementary context shows broad semiconductor weakness, while the 10-year yield is near 4.85% and Brent is near $102.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours, published Tail peaked at 43% during the September 9 U.S. selloff, then fell into the high teens and low twenties as two-way trade returned. The September 9 12:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and remains unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours concentrate risk around 12:30 UTC PPI and claims, the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and 14:00 UTC home sales. Oracle reports after the close. Extreme Stress persists from oil and yields, while Tail escalation remains conditional on observed persistent extension or failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: Delayed September NQ is 29,396.25, about 52.5 points below prior settlement but roughly 37 points above the session low. The rebound off 29,359.25 shows mean reversion remains present, while weak semiconductors, higher yields and oil keep Tail at the top of WATCH.
drivers: NQ remains above the session low after an earlier rebound
All seven tracked semiconductor names are lower in fresh Finviz context

forecast.analysis: PPI and initial claims are scheduled for 12:30 UTC within this hour. Tail remains at the top of WATCH because event importance alone is not a block; persistent post-release extension or failed retracements would be required for escalation.

The first post-release hour leads into the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open. WATCH remains conditional unless the data impulse survives meaningful pullbacks and repeatedly extends through the opening auction.

The cash-open hour also contains Existing-home sales at 14:00 UTC. Tail remains WATCH unless the post-PPI/open move holds near an extreme and defeats meaningful retracements with cross-asset confirmation.

By this hour the PPI, cash-open and home-sales checkpoints are behind. Tail eases slightly if two-way rotation is established; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would keep the danger window active.

With the main U.S. data window behind, conditional Tail declines if NQ rotates away from session extremes. Elevated oil and Treasury yields can sustain extreme Stress without implying a pathological one-way price path.
drivers: Oil and Treasury yields remain macro stressors

forecast.analysis: As the U.S. session moves toward midday, Tail stays in lower WATCH if countertrend rotations retain depth. High oil and yields keep Stress extreme, but repeated shallow pullbacks would be needed for renewed Tail escalation.
drivers: Oil and Treasury yields remain elevated

forecast.analysis: Midday liquidity can amplify swings, but Tail remains below the blocking threshold when countertrend moves retain depth. A sequence of shallow pullbacks and fresh extensions would be the relevant adverse change.
Late-day structure becomes the focus. A balanced range would keep Tail near the lower WATCH band, while directional efficiency into the final hours would prevent further easing.

Approaching the U.S. power-hour transition, Tail remains WATCH only because elevated macro stress can magnify any renewed directional move. The forecast still assumes no confirmed persistent extension.

Power-hour risk is conditional on actual continuation rather than the clock alone. Meaningful countertrend rotations would support stable WATCH risk; repeated extensions with shallow pullbacks would keep risk elevated.
Oracle's after-close earnings cycle adds technology-specific headline risk. Tail is kept in WATCH conditionally because an earnings catalyst is not itself evidence of a one-way NQ path.
drivers: Oracle fiscal Q1 2027 results after the U.S. close

forecast.analysis: After the main corporate catalyst window, Tail eases if index futures absorb headlines with two-way trade. Stress remains extreme because energy and rates conditions can stay restrictive overnight.
Early overnight trade is expected to be thinner. In the absence of persistent extension, Tail falls back to low while Stress remains extreme from the macro backdrop.
The overnight forecast keeps Tail low unless a new geopolitical or rates shock produces directional persistence. Two-way trade remains the baseline conditional structure.
Tail remains low under a conditional two-way overnight path. A fresh extreme held through several shallow pullbacks would be the specific condition that would invalidate this easing.

The late U.S. overnight window retains low Tail while Stress stays extreme. No future directional path is assumed; risk would rise only with confirmed persistent extension or a discontinuous catalyst.

As Asian trading develops, low Tail remains conditional on continued mean-reverting structure. Cross-asset alignment would matter only if independent NQ evidence also showed persistent directional efficiency.
The Asian-session forecast keeps Tail low if countertrend swings remain meaningful. Semiconductor weakness remains contextual and does not by itself establish a live NQ trend.
Ahead of the European transition, Tail stays low under balanced price discovery. A new energy or rates shock could raise Stress further without automatically changing Tail.

European participation can widen the range, but low Tail remains appropriate unless directional extension persists through retracement attempts. Stress stays extreme in the high-oil, high-yield backdrop.
drivers: Retracement quality after any range expansion

forecast.analysis: As Europe becomes fully active, Tail returns to WATCH because Friday's CPI is approaching, but this remains event-proximity risk rather than evidence that a future one-way move has occurred.
Pre-U.S. positioning ahead of Friday CPI can increase sensitivity to rates and oil. Tail remains WATCH conditionally; only observed persistent extension would justify moving into a blocking band.
The final forecast hour remains before Friday's CPI release. Tail stays in WATCH as event sensitivity rises, while the forecast does not assume the release outcome or any post-release price path.
drivers: CPI is scheduled after this forecast horizon at 12:30 UTC
No future release outcome is assumed
